title: Service Reliability Catalyst: 60-Day Activation Plan
content:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic 60-day plan to operationalize SLOs and shared reliability contracts across product, platform, and SRE. This is a working activation playbook — not final. Use as a sprint kit for service teams launching model-serving or major throughput-sensitive features.

Context / problem statement:
- Multiple feature teams have different priors about acceptable latency and error behavior. Lack of consistent SLO contracts causes noisy oncall, unclear rollbacks, and uneven error budget usage.
- Platform and Dedicated infra need explicit gating for autoscale, KV-cache warmup, and fallback policies.
- We need a short, repeatable activation cycle that pairs SRE with product owners and platform engineers to ship meaningful SLOs and automated checks.

Success criteria (end of 60 days):
- 4 pilot services have published SLOs with agreed owners and SLA translation notes.
- Each pilot has a short runbook (1 page) with escalation path & one automated smoke test.
- Error budget dashboard created in Console for pilots, with alerting thresholds and a weekly review ritual.
- One cross-team rollback/fallback policy template available for product teams.

High-level approach:
- Phase 0 (prep, week -1 to 0): design SLO contract template + decision checklist. Stoplight: green = ready to pilot.
- Phase 1 (weeks 1–2): discovery & measurement wiring (traces, metrics, synthetic tests).
- Phase 2 (weeks 3–6): SLO drafting, negotiation, and automated gating (alerts, dashboards).
- Phase 3 (weeks 7–8): launch, observe, retrospective, and playbook handoff.

Roles and responsibilities (owner assignments for pilot run):
- Program lead: Aisha Patel — coordinator, exec updates, cross-team unblock.
- SRE partner: Diego Morales — measurement design, alerts, runbooks.
- Platform lead: Claire Nguyen — autoscale/fallback configs, infra gating.
- Product sponsor: Jenna Liu — business impact, rollback authority.
- Observability engineer: Samir Rao — dashboard + synthetic test authorship.

Artifacts to produce (minimum viable set):
1) SLO contract template (one-paragraph service description, golden metrics: p99 latency, 95th CPU-util, success rate).
2) 1-page runbook per service (who to page, how to run smoke tests, quick mitigation steps).
3) Console dashboard tile + alert rules (error budget burn > 10%/day, sustained p99 degradation 3x baseline).
4) Synthetic smoke test harness in CI (lightweight traffic replay, KV-cache warmup step).
5) Fallback/rollback policy template (feature flags + model variant fallback matrix).

Sprint schedule (compact calendar):
- Week 0 (kickoff): 60-min cross-functional kickoff, present template, pick pilots.
- Week 1: measurement wiring; SRE + Observability pair to hook metrics and traces for pilot services.
- Week 2: define SLO targets and initial alerts; product and SRE negotiate burn rate windows.
- Week 3: implement synthetic smoke tests; platform config review for autoscale and cache warmup.
- Week 4: create dashboards and connect alerting to escalation path; tabletop run of rollback policy.
- Week 5: run early traffic test under controlled burn; monitor error budget signals; iterate SLO thresholds.
- Week 6: finalize contracts, signoffs from product + platform; freeze runbooks.
- Week 7: gradual launch to prod (canary) with SLO monitoring; enforce rollback policy.
- Week 8: 1-week observation window, retro, and handoff to oncall rotations.

Tactical checklists (copyable):
- Pre-kickoff checklist: identify service owner, current p99/p95 baseline, top two error types, existing alerts.
- Measurement checklist: ensure request/response traces include model variant id, latency bucket tag, and success boolean; synthetic test includes KV cache priming.
- Alert checklist: separate alert for signal degradation vs. error budget burn; paging only on escalation conditions (not noise).

Experimental features & probes (things to try in pilots):
- Latency fuzz testing: introduce small CPU delays in non-prod to exercise tail latency behavior.
- Error budget grazing session: scheduled 30-minute controlled regression to validate alerting and rollback.
- Autoscale cold-start probe: simulated spike on canary to validate scale-up latency and cache warmup impact.

Communications plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync: Tuesday 10:00am (Status, blockers, action owners).
- Weekly digest: short summary to #reliability-updates and product sponsors (what was observed, decisions made).
- Escalation: page SRE lead if error budget burn > 20% in 24h OR p99 > target * 3 for 10 minutes.

Risk register / open issues:
- Risk: Inconsistent tagging of model variants will make per-variant SLOs impossible. Mitigation: must include model_variant tag in traces before week 2. Owner: Product infra.
- Risk: Feature teams resist binding SLOs (fear of rollback). Mitigation: use experiment runbooks and negotiated burn windows; start permissive and tighten. Owner: Program lead.
- Open question: what SLA-to-SLO translation will sales/finance require for Dedicated customers? Action: brief GTM, due by week 3.

Automation & CI integration notes:
- Synthetic smoke tests should run nightly in staging and on each canary roll; pass/fail should be pushed as a single boolean to the Console events stream.
- Add a lightweight check in the release pipeline that validates required tags and metrics are present; block rollout if missing.

Handbook / templates (where to find them):
- SLO contract template: Confluence link (see linked_artifacts).
- Runbook template: short checklist + escalation matrix (to be created under ops-playbooks repo).

Metrics to report to leadership (weekly):
- Number of pilot services with SLOs published (target 4).
- Mean time to rollback decision when alert fires (target < 30m for pilot).
- Error budget consumption rate per pilot (trend).
- Number of false positive pages during pilot (target <= 1/week).

Retrospective agenda (end of 60 days):
- What assumptions were wrong?
- Which parts of template reduced friction? Which increased friction?
- Playbook updates and next 90-day recommendation (scale to 8–12 services).

Next steps (immediately after kickoff):
- Aisha: confirm pilot list and send calendar invites (by EOD).
- Diego: baseline measurements for selected pilots (run in 24–48h).
- Claire: prepare autoscale + cache warmup checklist for platform review.
- Jenna: prepare business-impact notes for each pilot (SLO tradeoffs).

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could experiment with a short-lived "SLO champion" rotation: 1 week per feature team where an SRE pairs full-time to unblock. Good for onboarding owners.
- Consider a lightweight scorecard for SLO readiness (tags present, dashboards wired, runbook < 1 page).
- Keep the first pass conservative: prefer observability and rollback precedence over hard-cut enforcement.

Appendix: quick SLO contract example (one-liner):
Service: inference-routing-api — description: routes generation requests, applies routing policy and caching.
SLOs (initial): request success rate 99.9% monthly; p99 latency < 600ms (95% of days). Error budget budgeted for 30% burn during big model rollouts with planned regression windows.

Document versioning: this is draft v0.3 — iterate after the first week's notes.
